newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN NEED 67 TO WIN AFTER ZIMBABWE COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN NEED 67 TO WIN AFTER ZIMBABWE COLLAPSE.

text.p: Incisive fast bowling by Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis and Shahid Nazir thrust Pakistan to the brink of victory over Zimbabwe in the second and final test on Saturday.
Zimbabwe, 134 behind on first innings, collapsed from their overnight 136 for three to 200 all out on the stroke of lunch on the third day.
Pakistan will begin their second innings after the interval needing just 67 to win and take the short series 1-0.
Zimbabwe lost their last seven wickets for 64 in the morning as Pakistan's formidable pace attack again wreaked havoc.
Captain Akram, who finished with 10 wickets in the match, triggered the collapse by removing David Houghton (74) on his first ball of the morning.
Nazir had Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell (51) caught behind on his fourth ball as the touring side lost their overnight pair without adding to the total.
Andy Flower offered brief resistance with a plucky 23 before he was taken at second slip by Saeed Anwar off Waqar.
Akram ended the innings by trapping Everton Matambanadzo leg before to finish with four for 57 while Waqar claimed four for 54. Nazir took two for 25.
